  • Smiles add little to self-expression if we are dull, sinister, or smug, they merely mirror the
  • inner self. (An) / (CO1)

  • • Used to describe the reading experience as organic, not purely rational (An) / (CO1)

questions.question: How does To Sir, with Love present teaching as a form of social work? Analyse with reference to Braithwaite’s role.
questions.solution_html:
• Braithwaite enters a school the system has written off; his mission is implicitly social
  • • Students are from deprived East End backgrounds; classroom = intervention space
  • • He addresses racism, poverty, and lack of aspiration directly
  • • Insists on dignity (formal address, hygiene, conduct) as tools of social uplift
  • • Builds relationships across racial difference — himself a Black professional in white
  • working-class space
  • • Teaching becomes consciousness-raising: students learn self-worth alongside curriculum
  • • His role blurs teacher/mentor/social worker/role model
  • • The ending (students' gift, Gillian's acceptance) confirms the social bond formed
  • (An) / (CO4)

questions.question: Discuss how Lamb uses the pseudonym "Elia" to merge his own personality with a fictionalized narrative.
questions.solution_html:
• "Elia" is a pseudonym taken from a real colleague but used as a fictional alter ego
  • • Allows Lamb to write autobiographically while maintaining ironic distance
  • • Personal memories (grandmother Field, his brother) appear but filtered through Elia's
  • voice
  • • The persona enables sentiment without sentimentality — emotion is managed through art
  • • Elia is both Lamb and not-Lamb: same memories, heightened literary sensibility
  • • Creates a layered narrator: reader knows the 'truth' behind the fiction
  • • The essays become a form of self-portraiture through indirection (An) / (CO1)

questions.question: In "Colour Bar", discuss how dignity and self - respect shape Kaunda’s political actions.
questions.solution_html:
• Kaunda's resistance to racial humiliation is rooted in personal dignity, not just ideology
  • • Refuses to internalise colonial definitions of inferiority
  • • Self-respect becomes a political stance: to remain dignified is to resist
  • • Evident in his encounters at the Chemist's shop and restaurant
  • • Personal experience of discrimination directly fuels his political vision; founded UNIP
  • (United National Independence Party)
  • • Dignity is framed as both a human right and a political foundation (An) / (CO2)

questions.question: Discuss the importance of the first-person narrator in giving shape to the story The Shape of the Sword. [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• The narrator is a stranger to whom the disfigured man (the Moon) tells his story
  • • Creates dramatic irony: reader senses the narrator may be complicit
  • • The twist — narrator IS the coward he has been condemning — depends on first-person
  • concealment
  • • First person allows the story to be a confession disguised as an accusation
  • • Reader is manipulated alongside the narrator-listener
  • • Borges uses the technique to question how identity and guilt are narrated
  • • The shape of the scar becomes the shape of the story (An) / (CO3)
  • (15x2=30)
